summary: Crash when set_ominous_bottle_amplifier item modifier sets out-of-range amplifier
description: Summary This is yet another "item modifier setting invalid component causing crash" bug. Here, the new set_ominous_bottle_amplifier item modifier does not clamp or validate the amplifier, causing a crash. Steps to Reproduce - Give yourself a stick. - Run the following command: /item modify entity @s hotbar.0 {function:"set_ominous_bottle_amplifier",amplifier:10} - Pause the game. Expected Result The game does not crash. Actual Result The game crashes.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Give yourself a stick.  
2. Run the command ``/item modify entity @s hotbar.0 {function:"set_ominous_bottle_amplifier",amplifier:10}``.  
3. Press **Esc** to pause the game.  
4. Observe that the game crashes.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 24w13a, 1.20.5 Pre-Release 1 (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior: When the command /item modify entity @s hotbar.0 {function:"set_ominous_bottle_amplifier",amplifier:10} is executed the game immediately terminates with a fatal error instead of applying the modifier, resulting in a complete crash that closes the world and displays a stack trace indicating an out‑of‑range amplifier value was processed without validation. The crash occurs regardless of whether the player is in single‑player or on a server and happens as soon as the command is submitted, preventing any further gameplay or command execution.
Expected Behavior: When the player gives themselves a stick and runs `/item modify entity @s hotbar.0 {function:"set_ominous_bottle_amplifier",amplifier:10}`, the item modifier should recognize that the amplifier value is outside the permitted range, clamp it to the highest allowed value (or reject it) and apply the resulting valid data to the stick without causing any error. The game should continue running normally.
